topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Unveiling Conic Sections
target_audience: High school geometry or early undergraduate calculus students

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Conic Anatomy
lecture_lines: A cone is defined by a vertex and circular base.
A plane cutting the cone creates a conic section.
Vary the plane angle to change the shape.
Circles transform into ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.
[Asset: cone_section_geometry]
animations: Draw a plane slicing the cone in #00FF00.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: Dandelin spheres fit perfectly inside a cone.
They are tangent to the cone in a circle.
Each sphere touches the cutting plane at one point.
These tangency points are the section's focal points.
[Asset: dandelin_sphere_setup]
animations: Place two Dandelin spheres inside the cone.
Show spheres touching the cone internally.

sections.title: The Geometric Proof: The Ellipse Case
lecture_lines: Consider the ellipse formed by the slicing plane.
The spheres touch the plane at two foci.
Distances to these points sum to a constant.
This proves the slice is indeed an ellipse.
[Asset: ellipse_proof_animation]
animations: Fade in a cross-section ellipse in #FFFFFF.
Draw distance lines from foci in #FF00FF.

sections.title: Visualizing Parabolas and Hyperbolas
lecture_lines: Parallel to the cone's side creates a parabola.
One sphere's point of tangency defines the focus.
Cutting through both nappes creates a hyperbola.
animations: Animate the plane tilting to create a parabola.
Animate the plane tilting further to create a hyperbola.
Fade in both curves simultaneously for comparison.

sections.title: Synthesis & Real-world Application
lecture_lines: Dandelin spheres connect 3D volume to 2D geometry.
They explain paths of comets and optics.
Geometry beautifully governs our physical universe.
animations: Display an architectural arch as a conic section.
Overlay the conic formula onto the arch.
Highlight the focus points on the arch.
